items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we'll learn how to compute inverses of reciprocal functions.

Content:
As an example, let's consider the function [MATH: f(x),] given by

Content:
[MATH: f(x) = \dfrac{7}{2x+4}.]

Content:
To find the inverse [MATH: f^{-1}(x),] we start by replacing [MATH: f(x)] with [MATH: y{:}]

Content:
[MATH: y = \dfrac{7}{2x+4}]

Content:
Now, interchanging [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] gives

Content:
[MATH: x = \dfrac{7}{2y+4}.]

Content:
Then, we make [MATH: y] the subject of the equation as follows:

Content:
[MATH: x|= (7)/(2y + 4); x(2y + 4)|= 7; 2xy + 4x|= 7; 2xy|= 7 − 4x; y|= (7 − 4x)/(2x)]

Content:
Therefore, the inverse function is
[MATH: f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{7 - 4x}{2x}.]

Now, interchanging [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] gives

[MATH: x = \dfrac{4}{(y-1)^2}.]

Then, we make [MATH: y] the subject of the equation, as follows:

[MATH: x|= (4)/((y − 1)^{2}); x ⋅ (y − 1)^{2}|= 4; (y − 1)^{2}|= (4)/(x); sqrt((y − 1)^{2})|= sqrt((4)/(x));|y − 1||= (2)/(sqrt(x)); y − 1|= (2)/(sqrt(x)); y|= (2)/(sqrt(x)) + 1]

Note that we used the fact that for [MATH: y > 1,] we have [MATH: |y-1| = y-1.]

Therefore, the inverse function is [MATH: f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} + 1.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:

Content:
[MATH: y = \dfrac{7}{2x+4}]

Content:
Now, interchanging [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] gives

Content:
[MATH: x = \dfrac{7}{2y+4}.]

Content:
Then, we make [MATH: y] the subject of the equation as follows:

[MATH: x = \dfrac{4}{(y-1)^2}.]

[MATH: |y-1| = y-1.]
